author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Diagnose a black PS2 FMV when its audio continues
summary: Reproduce one exact cutscene from a full boot, prove whether decoded video reaches software output, check the disc image independently, and separate IPU, renderer, field-order, and stale-state failures.
heroAlt: PCSX2 image-processing example from a PS2 title that exercises IPU color conversion during video playback

sourceLabels.pcsx2-whats-new-16: PCSX2 account of IPU color conversion and FMV-specific fixes
sourceLabels.pcsx2-video-playback: PCSX2 background on IPU decoding and FMV playback behavior

blocks.text: Prove that the black interval belongs to the movie path

Audible dialogue over a black image suggests that the emulated program is still advancing, but it does not by itself identify the missing stage. The PS2 Image Processing Unit decodes MPEG-related data, transfers and color-converts frames, and the graphics path presents them with a video mode and field order. A damaged or incomplete image can also supply audio while reads for video sectors fail. Choose a cutscene reachable quickly from an ordinary in-game save. Note the exact frame where picture disappears, whether subtitles or HUD remain visible, whether playback ends normally, and whether gameplay renders after the movie.
Do not use a skip-FMV patch as the first diagnostic step. It bypasses the failing workload and can turn a reproducible video defect into an unexplained story or loading transition.

items: A normal game save immediately before the same non-interactive cutscene; avoid emulator save states during baseline tests.
A verified personal disc image with its format and hash recorded, plus access to the original disc for redumping if verification fails.
Default emulation speed, automatic deinterlacing, native internal resolution, system GPU driver, and game patches disabled.
A timestamped note of picture, audio, subtitle, and post-movie behavior from two full boots.
Enough free storage for a short direct recording and the application log covering the transition.

blocks.text: Trace decode, transfer, and presentation in order

items: 1. Fully close the emulator, start the title through the normal boot path, load the in-game save, and record the entire transition into the movie.
2. Repeat the cold boot once before changing settings; compare the exact black-frame timestamp and whether audio timing is identical.
3. Change only the supported hardware API, restart again, and observe whether the first decoded picture appears while the rest of the profile stays fixed.
4. If hardware paths remain black, use software rendering for this short sequence and record whether it displays video, subtitles, and correct color.
5. When software shows the movie, return to the more stable hardware API and test deinterlacing separately only if a picture exists but fields are blank, alternating, or vertically displaced.
6. When software is also black, run the repository's accepted integrity workflow against the image and redump the owned disc if hashes or read logs are suspect.
7. Inspect the application log for read errors, IPU-related faults, renderer loss, or patch activation at the movie timestamp without sharing private storage paths.
8. After one branch restores picture, watch the full clip and the transition back to gameplay twice from fresh launches before saving the per-game result.

blocks.text: Audio and video streams can continue through different emulated units and buffers, so sound proves progress rather than successful picture decode. Software rendering distinguishes a hardware presentation problem from a broader IPU, timing, patch, or data problem. Independent image verification matters because optical-disc damage can be localized: menu and gameplay sectors may read while a movie's video sectors do not. Cold boots exclude stale decoder and save-state state that can survive a convenient retry.
A passing result covers the complete audiovisual sequence, not merely its first visible frame.

items: Video begins on the same beat as audio and remains visible through scene cuts and fades.
Subtitles and overlays appear in their intended layer rather than behind a black rectangle.
Color conversion is plausible, with no solid green, indexed-color corruption, or alternating blank fields.
The movie ends normally and control returns without a hang, accelerated audio, or skipped loading event.
Two independent cold boots pass with the verified image and the documented per-game profile.

blocks.text: FMV evidence that narrows the next report

items: Every copy made from the same scratched disc fails verification at matching sectors: preserve logs and replace the working image only from a legal clean master.
Software shows video but both hardware APIs lose it: attach renderer and driver details to a graphics report rather than changing CPU timing.
The picture works only after an emulator save-state load: discard that result and reproduce from the in-game save.
The movie is correct but the following level is black: diagnose the gameplay transition as a separate rendering or loading problem.

blocks.text: Re-enable automatic deinterlacing, select the original hardware renderer and system driver, remove experimental FMV or timing fixes, and restart from the in-game save. Quarantine any image that did not pass integrity checks; do not keep it in the active library simply because a skip patch reaches gameplay.
Short legal evidence is enough for a report

FMV footage is copyrighted game content. Record only the brief section needed to show the black-frame transition where local law and the support channel permit it. A serial, hash status, timestamp, log excerpt, and settings comparison are usually more actionable than uploading an entire cutscene.
